about: What this member said on the floor, from the Congressional Record: their own words only, and of those the sentences that name an alignment question's phrases or make a commitment. Written by npm run record:collect (scripts/collect-record.mjs).
name: LaMonica McIver

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: YOUNG MOTHERS IN CONGRESS
statements.title: YOUNG MOTHERS IN CONGRESS
sentences: The Life Time gym in Arlington has more accessible childcare than Congress and a shorter wait list.
It has been 53 years, and we still can't vote by proxy after giving birth.
Our voices belong here, and we are going to use them. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ENSURING SBA IMPLEMENTATION OF GAO RECOMMENDATIONS ACT OF 2026
statements.title: ENSURING SBA IMPLEMENTATION OF GAO RECOMMENDATIONS ACT OF 2026
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong support of my bill, H.R. 10371, the Ensuring SBA Implementation of GAO Recommendations Act of 2026, a commonsense, bipartisan bill that I am proud to lead alongside my wonderful Ranking Member Velazquez of New York.
Mr. Speaker, I urge members to support my bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FOURTH ANNIVERSARY OF THE TOPS SUPERMARKET SHOOTING IN BUFFALO, NEW YORK
statements.title: FOURTH ANNIVERSARY OF THE TOPS SUPERMARKET SHOOTING IN BUFFALO, NEW YORK
sentences: Across the aisle, people refuse to accept that an 18 year old should not have access to a military grade firearm.
Buffalo is a painful reminder of the racism and gun violence crisis affecting all of our Nation.
We stand with Congressman Kennedy who is their voice here.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: WOMEN'S HISTORY MONTH
statements.title: WOMEN'S HISTORY MONTH
sentences: It is the example of the Black women leaders that came before me that remind me that we cannot back down.
I am saying it plain: Black women are under attack, but we are not going to be silenced or scared--not now, not ever.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA POLICING PROTECTION ACT
statements.title: DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA POLICING PROTECTION ACT
sentences: The bills proposed by my Republican colleagues will worsen the already rampant injustices we see in the criminal justice system, make law enforcement more dangerous, and steal the futures of many of our youth.
D.C. has done this in part by having a police force that looks like the very people it is sworn to protect, lives in the community it serves, and caters to the unique needs of D.C. residents.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to vote ``no.''

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TRUMP'S LABOR AGENDA: UNSAFE AND UNDERPAID
statements.title: TRUMP'S LABOR AGENDA: UNSAFE AND UNDERPAID
sentences: Mr. Speaker, home health aides are some of the most essential workers in our economy, taking care of our parents and grandparents as they age and ensuring that sick and disabled people can live with dignity.
It is downright despicable that this administration has proposed to reverse the rule requiring that these vital workers be paid the Federal minimum wage.
This reckless rollback threatens the dignity, wages, and basic rights of nearly 4 million of our lowest paid and most essential workers, the majority of whom are women and women of color.
It is rooted in a despicable framework that sees farmworkers, particularly those from other countries and those that are Black and Brown, as disposable.
Mr. Speaker, I yield to the gentlewoman from Minnesota (Ms. Omar) to discuss the tools available to OSHA to keep Americans safe at work.
As my colleagues have mentioned, they even want to bring back the cruel, outdated policy of allowing employers to pay disabled workers less than minimum wage, often pennies on the dollar.

From healthcare workers, many of them women and women of color, at risk of losing minimum wage and overtime protections; to construction workers who could now be forced to operate in unsafe conditions with no guarantee of adequate lighting or visibility standards; to farmworkers who already endure grueling conditions are being stripped of hard- fought protections.
We will not let them get away with it.
If the Secretary will not act, we will take matters into our own hands.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: BETTER IS POSSIBLE
statements.title: BETTER IS POSSIBLE
sentences: I spoke to families who told me that they didn't know how they would be able to afford healthcare once their Medicaid is cut, once the effective date kicks in.

Mr. Speaker, we must and will oppose attempts to slash those services, and we won't support a partisan, poisonous bill that hurts the people we serve and the people who depend on us, the people who have elected us to work on their behalf and their behalf only.
We will not support it, point-blank, period.
That is why we are going to continue to fight like hell for the people we serve because we know that they deserve better.
We will not stop fighting, no matter what.
We are fighting not just to pass something to keep the lights on for another few months but for a solution that actually serves the American people, something that makes people's lives better.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF SENATE AMENDMENT TO H.R. 1, ONE BIG BEAUTIFUL BILL ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I ask unanimous consent to amend the rule to make in order the amendment at the desk that protects against any cuts to Medicaid and SNAP.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: AMERICAN ENTREPRENEURS FIRST ACT OF 2025
statements.title: AMERICAN ENTREPRENEURS FIRST ACT OF 2025
sentences: Let me remind my colleagues on the other side that those issues would be inflation, access to capital, workforce shortages, and the lingering effects of--guess what, drumroll--tariffs.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong opposition to H.R. 2966, a bill that does not serve our small business community, despite its name.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to vote ``no'' on this bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SAVE SBA FROM SANCTUARY CITIES ACT OF 2025
statements.title: SAVE SBA FROM SANCTUARY CITIES ACT OF 2025
sentences: Targeting sanctuary cities, as this bill does, is beyond the scope of the SBA's duties.
I urge Members to vote ``no'' on the Save SBA from Sanctuary Cities Act of 2025 to protect the SBA's mission and vibrant economies for all of our cities.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: 7(a) LOAN AGENT OVERSIGHT ACT
statements.title: 7(a) LOAN AGENT OVERSIGHT ACT
sentences: Second, by requiring information on loan performance, default rates, and risk analysis, it gives Congress the data we need to do our jobs, making sure the 7(a) program works as intended, and protects small business owners.
They reinvest, and they show us what is possible in our communities.

Mr. Speaker, I rise today in support of H.R. 1804, commonsense and bipartisan legislation, which I am proud to co-lead with my colleague, Congressman Meuser, to bring better oversight and real accountability to one of the Small Business Administration's most important loan programs, 7(a).
I urge my colleagues to support this bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NATIONAL GUN VIOLENCE AWARENESS MONTH
statements.title: NATIONAL GUN VIOLENCE AWARENESS MONTH
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today to speak on an issue that has devastated families and communities across this country: gun violence.
For years, gun violence has been an unchecked epidemic.
We will continue to demand comprehensive gun reform, background checks, closing loopholes, and a ban on assault weapons because our lives and our children's lives depend on it.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: GOP TAX SCAM HURTS WOMEN AND FAMILIES
statements.title: GOP TAX SCAM HURTS WOMEN AND FAMILIES
sentences: Mr. Speaker, ``I probably wouldn't be alive because I wouldn't have been able to afford [my] medicine.'' That is what Dominique from East Orange, New Jersey, said about Medicaid.
Dominique is one of the 100,000 Americans who lives with the sickle cell disease, and she is one of the millions of Americans who would be devastated by Republicans gutting Medicaid.
That is also when her aunt enrolled her in Medicaid.
Medicaid didn't mean that life was easy--Dominique spent much of her time in hospitals and visiting doctors--but it made life possible.

With Medicaid, she is able to see a hematologist regularly, receive the appropriate equipment and medications to make living at home possible, seek mental health care due to the toll of living with this disease, and receive treatment for any potential emergencies.
Dominique gets to live knowing the care she deserves is within her reach, in her own words, thanks to Medicaid. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: EDUCATION IS OF GREAT IMPORTANCE TO CONGRESSIONAL BLACK CAUCUS, CONGRESS, AND CONSTITUENTS
statements.title: EDUCATION IS OF GREAT IMPORTANCE TO CONGRESSIONAL BLACK CAUCUS, CONGRESS, AND CONSTITUENTS
sentences: When we defund education, we are defunding hope.

I have often said that education is the one thing no one can take away from you, but right now Trump and his billionaire buddies are trying to take away the very structure that ensures our kids get that education in the first place.
I cosponsored H.R. 433, the Department of Education Protection Act, to prohibit the use of congressional appropriated funds for any reorganization or dismantling of the Department of Education.

I urge my colleagues across the aisle in this room to fight for our schools, fight for our teachers, fight for every child who dares to dream beyond their circumstances because they are watching, and they are counting on us.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: INVESTING IN MAIN STREET ACT OF 2025
statements.title: INVESTING IN MAIN STREET ACT OF 2025
sentences: I urge my colleagues to support this bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: BLACK HISTORY MONTH
statements.title: BLACK HISTORY MONTH
sentences: Our hard-fought progress is threatened by the racist agenda pushed forward by this administration, but we will not back down.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: "WE WERE STRANGERS ONCE, TOO"
statements.title: "WE WERE STRANGERS ONCE, TOO"
sentences: It is time to bring SNAP up to speed and create opportunities for working families to use essential programs like SNAP that reduce poverty and help them make ends meet.
By getting rid of the shelter cap, this bill ensures working families who are spending too much on rent and utilities get the benefits they deserve without being punished by high housing costs.

Making SNAP More Accessible Madam Speaker, I introduced the SNAP Benefits Fairness Act in the U.S. House with Representative Shontel Brown to remove the housing cap on the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program and make SNAP benefits more accessible to those who need them.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: COMBATING PREVENTABLE AMPUTATIONS
statements.title: COMBATING PREVENTABLE AMPUTATIONS
sentences: The ARC Act will save lives and reduce amputations by ensuring high- risk Medicare and Medicaid recipients have access to PAD screenings at no additional cost.
Every Kid is at Risk Mr. Speaker, I rise to object to the dangerous bill, H.R. 28, the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act of 2025, better known as the child predator empowerment act.
With the co-leadership of Representatives Jonathan Jackson and Robin Kelly, I am proud to introduce the ARC Act to save limbs, reduce patient costs, and save lives.
